parchment.$description: Parchment — Page canvas, body text on dark panels — a warm desaturated cream that makes the dark editorial cards feel inset rather than overlaid

ash.$description: Ash — Hairline borders, dividers, subtle surface separators — the workhorse neutral that defines the 1px structural rhythm across the page

smoke.$description: Smoke — Secondary borders and muted structural lines where Ash is too present

silver.$description: Silver — Input borders and disabled-state surfaces

ink.$description: Ink — Primary text, icon strokes, and the darkest borders on light surfaces

bone.$description: Bone — Reverse text on dark panels, card surfaces, and icon fills on dark backgrounds

olive-charcoal.$description: Olive Charcoal — Warm editorial panel surface (left card) and primary action background — a dusty olive-black that distinguishes DrawHistory's signature dark from generic #111

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Deep display panel surface (right card) and button background — the second editorial tone, slightly cooler and deeper than Olive Charcoal

saffron-dot.$description: Saffron Dot — Sole chromatic accent — announcement indicators and small functional punctuation only. Never used for fills, buttons, or large areas

eloquia-text.$description: Primary typeface across all UI text. Weight 300 in uppercase at display sizes (55–104px) creates the signature hushed editorial tone — the same approach as museum wall labels, where the label's weight is anti-authoritarian and confident. Body copy uses weight 400 at 16–18px. The negative tracking tightens as size increases, compressing display headlines while keeping body text optically normal.

roboto-mono.$description: Monospace label typeface for technical or meta annotations — small captions, metadata, button labels in outlined buttons. Its geometric monospaced rhythm contrasts with Eloquia's editorial proportions, providing a secondary voice for system-level information.
